name: Reputation as capital

subjectOf.text: Kaal stipulates the core proposition of reputation as capital: once meaningful decentralized reputation is established, reputation can be used to remove the need for a capital base and for capital requirements.
subjectOf.abstract: In essence, once meaningful decentralized reputation is established, reputation can be used to remove the need for capital base and/or capital requirements.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Reputation as Capital – How DAOs Upgrade Finance (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3949098
scope_conditions: meaningful decentralized reputation has been established

subjectOf.text: The more reputation replaces capital, the less capital must be allocated, tied and encumbered, which raises the ratio of unencumbered capital available to be newly deployed.
subjectOf.abstract: The more reputation replaces capital the less capital has to be allocated, tied, and encumbered. In turn, the ratio of capital becoming unencumbered through reputation increases the deployment of capital ratio, e.g. a higher proportion of unencumbered capital can be newly encumbered.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Reputation as Capital – How DAOs Upgrade Finance (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3949098
scope_conditions: reputation is encumbered and tied to an asset in place of capital

subjectOf.text: Misjudging the public commitment portion of a firm underwriting engagement would neutralize the liquidity the DAOIC previously gained through reputation staking.
subjectOf.abstract: Getting the public commitment part on a firm underwriting engagement wrong would neutralize the prior gained liquidity from RNFT staking.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Reputation as Capital – How DAOs Upgrade Finance (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3949098

subjectOf.text: Replacing capital with reputation increases liquidity because reputation takes over part of the role of capital and frees otherwise locked capital, letting decentralized investment vehicles deploy capital more effectively since reputation staking on deals requires no capital deployment.
subjectOf.abstract: When reputation takes over part of the role of capital it frees up otherwise locked capital that cannot fully be utilized. Decentralized investment vehicles are able to deploy capital more effectively because reputation staking on deals does not require the deployment of capital.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Reputation as Capital – How DAOs Upgrade Finance (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3949098
scope_conditions: decentralized investment vehicles using reputation staking

subjectOf.text: Decentralized reputation governance models in venture capital have the potential to upgrade the venture capital market.
subjectOf.abstract: This article shows that decentralized reputation governance models in venture capital have the potential to upgrade the venture capital market.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, REPUTATION AS CAPITAL – How Decentralized Autonomous Organizations Address Shortcomings in the Ventu (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3962614

subjectOf.text: The novelty of reputation as capital lies in the decentralized and democratized capital allocation functionality enabled by the DAO design.
subjectOf.abstract: The novelty of "Reputation as Capital" lies in the decentralized and democratized capital allocation functionality enabled by the DAO design.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, REPUTATION AS CAPITAL – How Decentralized Autonomous Organizations Address Shortcomings in the Ventu (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3962614
scope_conditions: a VC DAO built on reputation tokens

subjectOf.text: If reputation whales stake reputation on a project and the market commits the capital for that stake, the whales should still receive part of the ROI because it is their reputation that is at stake, and they are not required to commit capital or to support capital calls with liquidity.
subjectOf.abstract: If whales stake but the market commits for their stake with capital, whales should still have the right to receive (part of) the ROI because it is their reputation that is at stake. Whales are not required to commit capital and don't have to support capital calls with liquidity.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, REPUTATION AS CAPITAL – How Decentralized Autonomous Organizations Address Shortcomings in the Ventu (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3962614
scope_conditions: whale reputation that has become meaningful through a track record

subjectOf.text: Reputation as venture capital must be distinguished from the capital replacement enabled in decentralized underwriting, because in venture capital reputation needs to fill the role of capital for each funded venture deal rather than only when a claim is filed.
subjectOf.abstract: reputation in venture capital needs to fill the role of capital for each funded venture deal.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, REPUTATION AS CAPITAL – How Decentralized Autonomous Organizations Address Shortcomings in the Ventu (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3962614
scope_conditions: comparison of decentralized underwriting and venture capital DAOs

subjectOf.text: Reputation as capital has the potential to lower capital requirements for VC businesses significantly and to increase liquidity at unprecedented levels, because VCs can sell their fungible reputation tokens to the market as needed.
subjectOf.abstract: Reputation as capital has the potential to lower capital requirements for VC businesses significantly and increase liquidity at unprecedented levels because VCs fungible reputation tokens can be sold to the market as needed by.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, REPUTATION AS CAPITAL – How Decentralized Autonomous Organizations Address Shortcomings in the Ventu (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3962614
